sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Lewisburg
sections.html:
Look for the Recorder of Deeds in the Union County Courthouse at 103 South Second Street, Lewisburg, PA 17837, or phone (570) 524-8762. One elected office holds both this job and the Register of Wills. Staff are at the counter from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., though the cutoff for recording documents is 4:15 p.m.

Those fifteen minutes catch people out. Arrive at 4:20 and the deed waits until the next day, so anyone who needs same-day recording should get there well ahead of the cutoff.

sections.h2: What the Union County recorder does
sections.html:
Paperwork tied to land and buildings goes on file here: deeds, mortgages, releases, easements and rights of way, subdivisions and restrictions. It also records notary and county officer information and military service discharges. Online searches cover January 1, 1962 forward. Anything older is on microfilm.

The recorder also collects the real estate transfer tax for the state, the townships, the boroughs and the school districts. It is the last stop in a sale. After buyer and seller sign at closing, the deed is recorded here and the taxes are paid in the same step.

A document that misses a requirement comes back unrecorded. If a mailed document cannot be recorded, it comes back with an explanatory letter and a $3.00 charge.

Union County filing and payment rules
Filing itemRequirement
Recording cutoff4:15 p.m. on business days
ChecksOne check per recorded document and one per transfer tax payment, payable to Union County Recorder of Deeds
Check amountExact amount, because no refunds are given
Statement of ValueTwo copies, fully completed, signed and dated, when one is required
Certificate of addressSigned, for the grantee, mortgagee or assignee on every deed, mortgage and mortgage assignment
Return by mailStamped, self-addressed envelope supplied at recording
  • Every acknowledgment needs the county, state and date, the names of the people or corporate officers who appeared, and the notary's signature, seal and expiration date.
  • A notary stamp has to be legible, and the stamp, seal and signature cannot overlap.
  • Re-recording a document takes new acknowledgments and a note explaining why.
  • Blanket documents are refused.

A recorder's fee schedule sits on the county website. What you owe turns on document type, pages and names. Because checks must match the fee to the penny, call (570) 524-8762 for your deed's exact total first.

The state also charges 1 percent of the property's value as transfer tax, and buyer and seller share the legal duty to pay it. The recorder forwards the state's part. Municipalities and school districts may add taxes of their own. Family transfers and inheritances passing by will or intestacy can be exempt.

Union County has 42,313 residents, 0.9 percent fewer than in 2020. Of its 16,372 homes and apartments, 72.3 percent are lived in by owners. A typical owned home is valued at $240,100, midpoint rent is $974 monthly and midpoint household income is $76,404.

Because 27.7 percent of homes are rented, you may be selling a house with a tenant in place. Put tenant terms in the sales contract, since the recorder's counter does not deal with them. Lewisburg is the county seat, and Hartleton, Mifflinburg and New Berlin are the other boroughs.

Rejected recordings usually trace back to the acknowledgment or the checks. The office is specific: a legible notary stamp, a seal that does not overlap the signature, a certificate of address and exact payment. Two sellers closing on the same day can have different outcomes because one deed had a clean notary block and the other did not.

When an estate sells the house, the Register of Wills in the same office handles probate and inheritance tax, with inheritance tax checks payable to Union County Register of Wills, Agent. An executor can often finish both errands in a single courthouse visit in Lewisburg.

Title companies record most sales. A seller who files personally needs the signed, notarized deed, the buyer's certificate of address, a Statement of Value if the full tax is not being paid, separate checks for the recording fee and each tax payment, and a stamped return envelope. One folder holding all of it keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Deed with a complete, legible notary block.
  • Signed certificate of address for the grantee.
  • Checks written to Union County Recorder of Deeds, one per document and per tax.
  • Statement of Value in duplicate, if it applies.

Sellers who would rather avoid showings and repairs can ask for a direct cash purchase and pick their own timeline. Recording works the same way in either case.

When a parent's house is being sold, two jobs often land at the same courthouse counter. The Register of Wills deals with probate and inheritance tax, and the Recorder takes the deed. Check that the person signing has clear authority over the estate before the title agent books a closing, and ask whether the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Transfers by will or intestacy can be exempt from the state transfer tax.

Bring the estate papers with you on the day of closing, along with a copy of the death-related documents your title agent asked for. If a notary block is wrong on an estate deed, you will lose time re-signing, and heirs who live far away make that more painful.

sections.h2: Common errors to check before you leave the house
sections.html:
• The notary's stamp is smudged or runs over the signature.
  • One check was written for everything instead of one per document and one per tax payment.
  • The check is for an estimated amount instead of the exact fee.
  • The Statement of Value was filed as a single copy.
  • No stamped envelope was included for the return.

Any one of these sends the package back, and a returned package costs you the fee and a day or more. Go through the list with your title agent the day before closing, and keep the cutoff in mind if you plan to deliver the package yourself.

sections.h2: How a sale reaches the recorder
sections.html:
At closing you sign the deed before a notary and the buyer signs the certificate of address. The title agent figures the recording fee and transfer tax, writes the separate checks and builds the package. It is delivered ahead of the 4:15 p.m. cutoff or mailed with a stamped return envelope. When the deed is recorded, the tax is settled and county records show the buyer as owner.

If you are mailing the package yourself, send it early. A document that cannot be recorded comes back with a letter and a $3.00 charge, and the delay can push past your closing date.

faqs.q: When does the Union County recorder stop taking documents?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:15 p.m. although the office stays open fifteen minutes longer. Later arrivals wait until the next business day.

faqs.q: Will the Union County office accept a deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, with a stamped, self-addressed envelope and the correct checks. A document that cannot be recorded is mailed back with a letter and a $3.00 fee.

faqs.q: How far back do Union County online records go?
faqs.a: Records from January 1, 1962 to the present can be searched online. Earlier records are on microfilm and are available through the office.
No. The recording requirements call for separate checks for each recorded document and for each realty transfer tax payment, all in the exact amount.

faqs.q: Which Union County office collects the transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds collects it for the state, townships, boroughs and school districts. The state rate is 1 percent, and local shares are added by the municipalities and districts.
